title: VendPoint Pooled Site Minimum — Desk Guidance
content:
For the VendPoint Industrial Vending Program the monthly minimum is tested per machine, except that when every machine at a ship-to that was active or suspended during the month allows site minimum pooling, the minimum is tested once for the site: the pooled site usage against the sum of those machines' minimum monthly usage.

A pooled site shortfall fee is computed with the shortfall fee rate and capped at the monthly fee cap of the machine with the largest minimum (on a tie, the lowest machine serial), and is charged once, on that machine.

Machines still inside their ramp-up months are left out of the pool and are not tested; a single machine that does not allow pooling makes every machine at that site test on its own.

### Terms used

- **Net vend value of a machine for a month**: the vend values of the machine dated in the calendar month, less the values of returns to the machine and vend error credits dated in that month; shrink and fees are excluded.
- **Pooled site usage**: the net vend value for the month added up over every machine at the ship-to that was active or suspended during the month.

### Points of judgement

| Machines at the ship-to during the month | Test |
|---|---|
| Every one allows pooling | One site test: pooled site usage against the total of their minimums |
| At least one does not allow pooling | Every machine at the site is tested on its own |
| A machine is inside its ramp-up months | That machine is left out of the pool and not tested |

### Hypothetical worked case

Two machines at one ship-to both allow pooling and are past ramp-up; their minimums are 2000.00 and 1250.00 USD (total 3250.00 USD) and their net vend values are 1500.00 and 1000.00 USD (pooled 2500.00 USD). The site falls 750.00 USD short. The fee is computed on that 750.00 USD shortfall with the shortfall fee rate, capped at the monthly fee cap of the machine with the 2000.00 USD minimum, and charged once, on that machine. Had either machine not allowed pooling, each would instead be tested on its own. All figures are invented for illustration.
